question:
The grouped data for the observation are as follows.

 
 

 Class:
 2-4
 4-6
 6-8
 
 

 Frequency:
 2
 1
 2
 
 

The population skewness:
solution:
The correct answer is **zero**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **skewness of a population** is a measure of its asymmetry and can be calculated as the third standardized moment of the distribution.
 
• A **skewness of zero** indicates that the distribution is symmetrical
 
 
• ie, meaning that the mean, median, and mode are equal and the data is evenly distributed on either side of the center. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• In the given data, here have 3 classes with the respective frequencies.
 
• However, it is not enough information to determine the skewness of the population.
 
• The skewness can be calculated using the formula which requires the mean, standard deviation and the individual values of the population data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In general, positive skewness indicates that the tail of the distribution on the right side is longer or fatter compared to the left side, and the mode is on the left side of the center.
 
• On the other hand, negative skewness indicates that the tail on the left side is longer or fatter and the mode is on the right side of the center.
 
• It is important to note that the skewness is sensitive to outliers, and even a small number of outliers can have a significant impact on the skewness calculation.
